cleanIntro: The Super Black Eagle 3 is INERTIA-driven, not gas-driven, and that changes what cleaning means. There is no gas piston, no gas ports and no gas cylinder to decarbon — the whole system is a spring between the bolt body and the rotating locking head. So the parts that matter are the bolt assembly, the firing mechanism in the trigger guard, and the bore. Benelli's own position is that this gun needs no special maintenance; what it needs is that the bolt and the trigger group do not stay clogged with residue. ⚠ This book branches by VERSION at one point in the strip: the 3" and 20-gauge guns separate the cover from the barrel assembly. Your row is the 12 GA 3½", which takes the unbranched sequence — the step below says so where it matters. Printed folios are cited; they run five behind the PDF page.

steps.title: Safety catch on — the red ring must disappear
steps.action: Press the safety button in the trigger guard until the RED RING is no longer visible. Red showing means it will fire; the check is visual and takes a second.
steps.prose: Benelli defines the safe state by what you cannot see rather than by which way the button points, which is the more reliable test on a gun that can be set up left- or right-handed.
steps.quote: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until its red ring, indicating firing position, is no longer visible (figs. 17-18).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Gun safety catch — p.8

steps.title: Open the bolt and eject the chambered shell
steps.action: With the safety engaged and the muzzle in a safe direction, rest the stock on your hip and pull the cocking lever back. The chambered round is extracted and thrown clear. Then ease the cocking lever forward to close the breech.
steps.quote:
1) Engage the safety catch; rest the stock on your hip and pull the cocking lever to open the bolt (fig. 23): the cartridge in the chamber is extracted and ejected from the gun.
2) Gently release the cocking lever to close the breech block (fig. 16).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Unloading — p.10

steps.title: Empty the magazine through the carrier latch
steps.action: Turn the gun over, push the carrier down and press the front part of the carrier latch sideways with your index finger. One shell drops into your hand per press — press again for each one until the tube is empty.
steps.prose: This is the SBE3's magazine-dump: the carrier latch is what holds the column, so releasing it once releases exactly one shell. Do not expect them to cascade.
steps.quote:
3) Reverse the gun, and, thrusting the carrier down, press sideways the carrier latch frontal part with your index finger (fig. 24).
4) The cartridges will be released one by one into your hand (fig. 25); the carrier latch must be pressed for each released cartridge.
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Unloading — p.10

steps.title: Prove chamber, carrier and magazine empty
steps.action: Before a single part comes off, confirm all three: the chamber, the carrier and the magazine. Benelli repeats this instruction at the head of every operation in the book, and it names the carrier specifically because a shell can sit on it with the chamber clear.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber, carrier and the magazine are unloaded! (Carefully read the instructions on gun loading and unloading).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance) — p.12
steps.warn: For safety reasons, check if by opening the bolt the shotgun is unloaded. Then close the bolt again.

steps.title: Lock the bolt open, then pull the cocking lever out
steps.action: Draw the cocking lever back until the bolt locks open. If it will not hold, move the cartridge drop lever as the manual's arrow shows and try again. Then pull the cocking lever straight out of the bolt with a firm tug — it is a friction fit, so it wants one decisive pull, not a series of tentative ones.
steps.quote:
1) Open the bolt by pulling back the cocking lever (fig. 19) until the bolt is locked open. Should the bolt fail to engage, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat the operation (fig. 6).

2) Pull the cocking lever off with a firm tug (fig. 27).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.12

steps.title: Fore-end cap off the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap from the front of the magazine tube and take it right off. Put it somewhere it cannot roll away — it is the single fastener holding the front of the gun together.
steps.caution: Especially after the first rounds, check that the fore-end cap is firmly tightened.
steps.quote: 3) Unscrew the fore-end cap and remove from magazine tube (fig. 28).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.12

steps.title: Barrel–cover–fore-end unit forward off the tube
steps.action: Rest the stock against your hip. Hold the stock-and-receiver unit in one hand and the barrel-cover-fore-end unit in the other, and pull the front assembly FORWARD until it comes completely off the magazine tube.
steps.prose: On this gun the barrel is not screwed or pinned — it slides on the tube and indexes into the receiver, which is why the whole front comes off as one piece.
steps.aside: NOTE: for 3” and 20-gauge versions, the cover is divided from the barrel assembly and must be separately disassembled from the receiver. The Super Black Eagle 3 in this row is the 12-gauge 3½" gun and takes the unbranched sequence above — if your shotgun is one of the other versions, that separate step applies to you and this one does not.
steps.quote: 4) While resting the stock against your hip, grab the stock-receiver unit with a hand and the barrel-cover-fore-end unit with the other hand (fig. 29). Pull the latter forward and completely off the tube magazine (fig. 30).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.12

steps.title: Separate the fore-end from the barrel
steps.action: Rotate the barrel-cover-fore-end unit in the direction the manual's arrow shows, then draw it off the barrel guide ring.
steps.quote:
5) Rotate the barrel-cover-fore-end unit in the

direction shown by the arrow (fig. 31) and

separate it from the barrel by pulling it out of

the barrel guide ring (fig. 32).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.12

steps.title: Ride the bolt forward against the recoil spring
steps.action: Take hold of the bolt assembly with one hand so you are countering the recoil spring, press the carrier button, and let the bolt come forward under control until the spring is no longer pushing on it. Do NOT let it fly.
steps.prose: This is the step that bites people. The recoil spring is live behind the bolt and the carrier button is what releases it; a hand on the bolt is the whole safety measure.
steps.quote: 6) While holding the bolt assembly with one hand (fig. 5) so as to counter-balance the thrust of the recoil spring, push the carrier button (fig. 16) and ease the bolt forward until the recoil spring no longer pushes it forward (fig. 33).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.13
steps.warn: The recoil spring is under compression behind the bolt. Keep a hand on the bolt through this step.

steps.title: Bolt assembly out along its guides
steps.action: Draw the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along the guides it runs on rather than lifting it out.
steps.quote: 7) Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides (fig. 34).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.13

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin, firing pin and spring
steps.action: Hold the firing pin and its spring in place with a thumb — they are sprung — then push out the firing pin retaining pin. Only once the retaining pin is clear do you release and remove the firing pin and spring.
steps.prose: Holding first, drifting second, is the order that stops the firing pin launching out of the bolt when the pin releases it.
steps.caution: The firing pin spring is compressed. Keep the firing pin captive under a thumb until the retaining pin is fully out.
steps.quote:
8) Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the 33 bolt assembly, while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place (fig. 35).
9) Remove the firing pin and firing pin spring from the bolt (fig. 36).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.13

steps.title: Locking head off the bolt — field strip complete
steps.action: Take the locking head rotating pin out of its seat, then lift the locking head off the bolt. That is the strip: cocking lever, fore-end cap, fore-end, barrel, bolt assembly, firing pin group and locking head.
steps.prose: The rotating locking head with its two lugs IS the inertia system's business end. Its stem and its lug faces are what you are about to clean.
steps.quote:
10) Remove the locking head rotating pin from its seat (fig. 37).
11) Remove the bolt locking head from the bolt (fig. 38).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Stripping procedure — p.13

steps.title: Bore after every outing
steps.action: Clean the barrel after use. The bores are chromium plated internally, so this is about removing fouling rather than fighting corrosion in the bore itself.
steps.aside: NB: all barrels are internally chromium plated.
steps.quote: 1) normal cleaning of the barrel after use;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Maintenance — p.11

steps.title: Firing mechanism — clean out the powder residue
steps.action: The hammer, trigger and the rest of the firing mechanism clog with powder residue and foreign matter. Clean and lubricate them periodically; this is the group that causes a failure to fire when it is dirty.
steps.quote:
2) the firing mechanism, consisting of hammer,

trigger, etc., may become clogged with any powder residuals (or foreign matters). Remove them by periodical cleaning or lubrication;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Maintenance — p.11

steps.title: Bolt assembly — dismantled, cleaned, lubricated
steps.action: The bolt collects the same residue and Benelli asks for it to be periodically taken apart, cleaned and lubricated — which is exactly the strip you have just done. Clean the locking head's lug faces, its stem, the firing pin channel and the firing pin itself.
steps.prose: On an inertia gun a gummy locking-head stem is the classic cause of short-stroking, because the spring between head and body has to move freely for the action to work at all.
steps.quote: 3) the bolt assembly may also become clogged with the same residuals over mentioned and therefore must be periodically dismantled, cleaned and lubricated;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Maintenance — p.11
steps.warn: The slanted surfaces on the locking head’s stem should not be visible when the bolt is correctly reassembled.

steps.title: Oil what corrodes — and keep solvents off the furniture
steps.action: Oil the parts exposed to the weather. Use Benelli oil on the receiver, bolt and barrel, and use products made for the job on the stock and fore-end — wood, technopolymer, camo and painted finishes are all damaged by solvent-bearing oils.
steps.quote: 4) to keep the gun in good order, oiling of the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion is recommended.
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Maintenance — p.11
steps.warn: Avoid that parts get in contact with oils containing solvents or chemical substances in general, which could alter or damage their surfaces.

steps.title: Choke and its seat, and the ammunition ceiling
steps.action: Before the barrel goes back on, deal with the choke and its seat per the manual's own Internal choke section, and confirm the barrel has a choke fitted at all. Then check what you are feeding it: this gun's ceiling is set by CHAMBER LENGTH, so read your own chamber and match the shell to it.
steps.prose: The SBE3 will take 2¾, 3 and 3½ inch shells, but the rule is the shell must not be longer than the chamber it goes in — which is a fact about your gun, not about the model.
steps.aside: NOTE: for maintenance of the choke and relative seat, carefully read the instructions in the “Internal choke” paragraph, page 20.
steps.quote: Correct functioning of the shotgun is only guaranteed with cartridges of a maximum length of 58 mm (2” 3/4 - 70 mm chamber), 66 mm (3” - 76 mm chamber) or 78 mm (3” 1/2 - 89 mm chamber).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE 3 — Warranty | Owner's Manual | Spare Parts — G0681501 - 01/2021 — Choice of ammunition — p.11
steps.warn: CAUTION: never use cartridges with a case longer than the chamber. Non-compliance to this rule would have serious consequences for both the shotgun and the shooter.

deepAbsentReason: The strip above IS Benelli's full published teardown for cleaning and maintenance — it already reaches the firing pin, the firing pin spring and the rotating locking head inside the bolt, which on most guides is deep-clean territory. Beyond it the manual documents only the trigger guard assembly's removal (Stripping procedure steps 13-14, printed p.14), and that page is set in two interleaved columns whose text cannot be quoted contiguously from the extraction this project verifies quotes against. Rather than paraphrase a procedure whose exact wording could not be reproduced, no deep branch is offered. Benelli's own framing is that this shotgun "requires no special maintenance" (Maintenance, p.11).

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Normal cleaning of the bore after every use.
Bores are internally chromium plated — clean fouling out, do not scour.
Deal with the internal choke and its seat per the manual's Internal choke section before refitting.

cleaning.name: Bolt assembly
tasks: Dismantle, clean and lubricate periodically — Benelli's instruction, not an option.
Locking head: clean both lugs, the stem and the rotating-pin seat.
Firing pin and firing pin spring out; clean the channel through the bolt body.
Lubricate lightly with Benelli oil; the inertia spring must move freely.

cleaning.name: Firing mechanism
tasks: Hammer, trigger and the rest of the group cleaned of powder residue and foreign matter.
Lubricate periodically. A clogged firing mechanism is the manual's own listed cause of a failure to fire.

cleaning.name: Receiver and exterior
tasks: Benelli oil on receiver, bolt and barrel for lubrication and protection.
Oil the parts exposed to atmospheric corrosion.
Stock and fore-end: products intended for wood, technopolymer, camo or painted finishes ONLY — no solvent-bearing oils.

reassembly: Locking head back onto the bolt, then the locking head rotating pin into its seat.
Firing pin and firing pin spring into the bolt, held in place while the firing pin retaining pin goes back in.
Check the bolt is right: the slanted surfaces on the locking head's stem should NOT be visible when it is correctly assembled.
Bolt assembly back into the receiver along its guides, and the bolt link must slide over the trigger guard as the manual shows.
Fore-end back onto the barrel through the barrel guide ring.
Barrel-cover-fore-end unit back onto the magazine tube and home into the receiver.
Fore-end cap on and firmly tightened — re-check it after the first rounds.
Cocking lever pushed back into the bolt.
Confirm a choke tube is fitted before firing.
fncheck: With the gun proven empty and the muzzle safe: press the carrier button and open the bolt by hand, then close it, and confirm the RED DOT on the cartridge drop lever is clearly visible — that is the hammer showing cocked. Cycle the bolt fully by hand several times and confirm it locks open and releases cleanly. Engage the safety and confirm the red ring on the button disappears. If the gun fails to fire in use, Benelli's own troubleshooting order is: check the safety catch, check there is a cartridge in the barrel, then check the firing mechanism and clean and lubricate it if necessary.
